en: The First Section of the Nārāyaṇottaratāpinī Upaniṣad:
The Blessed Lord Brahmā said: "One who knows Brahman as bliss becomes one whose very nature is Being-Consciousness-Bliss."
Two birds, inseparable companions, cling to the same tree.
Of these two, one eats the sweet fruit, while the other looks on without eating.
That which is declared as the sound at the beginning of the Vedas and established at the end of the Vedas— He who is beyond that [sound] which has dissolved into its source is Maheśvara.
Smaller than the smallest, greater than the greatest, the Self is hidden in the cave of this living being;
free from sorrow, one beholds that Lord, the Greatness, who is without ritual action, through the grace of the Creator.
Indeed, the three worlds are perfumed by the fragrance of Vāsudeva;
you are the abode of all beings—O Vāsudeva, salutations be unto you!

The earth is Nārāyaṇa; the atmosphere is Nārāyaṇa; the heavens are Nārāyaṇa; the great world is Nārāyaṇa; the world of generation is Nārāyaṇa; the world of austerity is Nārāyaṇa; and truth is Nārāyaṇa. Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman. Nārāyaṇa alone is all this; there is nothing whatsoever other than Nārāyaṇa. Truth, knowledge, infinite is Brahman—He who knows Him hidden in the cave of the heart, in the highest heaven. From this very Self, indeed, space was produced; from space, air.

From wind comes fire; from fire, water; from water, earth; from earth, plants; from plants, food; from food, the person. Nārāyaṇa is indeed this entire supreme Brahman, the person within all persons. Nārāyaṇa is the Self, the inner ruler of all beings. This whole world is Nārāyaṇa, the Self. Nārāyaṇa is self-luminous; therefore, He is the essence of light.
Thin like the awn of wild rice, yellow, radiant, and resembling a minute atom—
within the center of that crest stands the Supreme Self.

Bound by the fetters, the individual soul (jīva) is considered transient; freed from the fetters, it is eternal. Just as rice is bound by its husk, yet becomes pure grain (taṇḍula) through the removal of that husk.
The Supreme Brahman, who is himself the Self, is remembered as Nārāyaṇa manifest;
he is the beginningless Nārāyaṇa, devoted to his yogic sleep.

That Great Soul, Nārāyaṇa, who is established at all times throughout the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, and who is devoted to supreme meditation— He who is the object of perception for all Vedāntas— is designated as Brahman.

The Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa said: "All this is established in Him alone; he who knows thus [attains the goal]. Thus ends the Upaniṣad. Thus, in the *Nārāyaṇottaratāpanīya*, the secret doctrine of the Atharvaveda, is the first section.
The second section: He, the Blessed Lord Brahmā, said: "It is known that Nārāyaṇa is the supreme reality."
Obeisance to you, O Nārāyaṇa, whose form is truth, consciousness, and bliss; who is infinite knowledge and immeasurable splendor; and whose very nature is the Supreme Brahman.
Obeisance be to you, Nārāyaṇa, who are eternally pure, awakened, eternal, of the nature of non-duality, blissful, and the very form of the Self.

Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, the glorious Nārāyaṇa, the Great Viṣṇu, possessed of immeasurable strength and prowess, the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace, accompanied by Lakṣmī, whose vehicle is Garuḍa, who has manifested in ten incarnations, the destroyer of all wicked Daityas and Dānavas, the protector of the righteous, whose form is the Supreme Brahman, the Great Soul, the Supreme Person, the lotus-eyed one, the Ancient Person, the pure and enlightened one, whose nature is Being-Consciousness-Bliss, the Great Soul, the radiant Sun, Āditya. Oṃ, salutation to Nārāyaṇa;
thousand-spoked, huṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Salutations again and again to Nārāyaṇa, the peaceful, the eternal, the enemy of Mura, the Lord of sacrifice, the sacrifice itself, and the refuge.
The blessed Brahmā said: "Nārāyaṇa is this entire universe; he who knows thus—this is the Upaniṣad."
Thus ends the second section in the Nārāyaṇottaratāpanīya, within the Atharvaṇa-rahasya.
Now begins the third section.

The blessed Lord Brahmā Nārāyaṇa said: "He who knows thus [knows] that he is the Supreme Brahman. It is taught that the entire Veda establishes Nārāyaṇa as the Self—the changeless, stainless Reality. That Nārāyaṇa becomes the Virāṭ Puruṣa; he becomes Vāsava among the gods; he becomes the mind among the senses; he becomes the primary Reality among all things. Oṃ! There is no mantra other than Nārāyaṇa, there is no worship other than Nārāyaṇa; nothing other than Nārāyaṇa is to be worshipped."

It is known that everything is indeed Nārāyaṇa. He who studies this constantly attains all desires. He becomes purified from the killing of a Brahmin; he becomes purified from the drinking of liquor; he becomes purified from the theft of gold; he becomes purified from violating the teacher’s bed; he becomes purified from approaching women who should not be approached; he becomes purified from eating what should not be eaten. He becomes purified from minor offenses and major sins. He becomes one who has studied all the Vedas.

One obtains the fruit of all sacrifices; one becomes a performer of all rites; one obtains the fruit of gifting the earth bounded by the four oceans; one becomes the best of the twice-born; one obtains the fruit of the four aims of life; as a student (*brahmacārī*), one becomes possessed of knowledge; as a householder (*gṛhī*), one possesses great sovereignty over sons and grandsons; and as a renunciant (*saṃnyāsī*), one attains liberation.
By either reading or even hearing it, one shall attain all desires.
By the grace of Nārāyaṇa, one attains the state of Vaikuṇṭha.
Thus spoke the Blessed One: "Whoever knows this thus. This is the Upaniṣad.
As many syllables of the Vedas as have been recited by the best of the twice-born, that many names of Hari have been proclaimed; of this there is no doubt.
O Nārāyaṇa, O Hari, O Kṛṣṇa, O Vāsudeva, O Teacher of the World! O Mukunda, O Acyuta, O Lord of Gods, O Mahāviṣṇu, salutations be unto You!
The elements are designated as "principles" (tattva), while the immutable is designated as the "imperishable" (akṣara);
and the Supreme Person is called Nārāyaṇa.
Thus ends the third section in the Nārāyaṇottaratāpanīya within the Atharvaṇa-rahasya.
Thus the Nārāyaṇottaratāpanīya Upaniṣad is complete.
